newsitem.title: BRAZIL: GM Brazil mum on Paraguay plant report.
newsitem.headline: GM Brazil mum on Paraguay plant report.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Brazilian unit refused to confirm or deny a local newspaper report that it hopes to build a $100 million automobile plant in neighboring Paraguay. "We do not confirm this report but we don't want to say 'No' either," Francisco Lellis, chief spokesman at General Motors do Brasil, told Reuters.
Lellis said the U.S. auto giant was "interested in factories in Paraguay, Uruguay and other places" but added he could not say if GM had settled on a plant in Paraguay.
Paraguay and Uruguay, along with Argentina and Brazil, are members of the four-nation Mercosur trade bloc.

Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil quoted Paraguayan Trade and Industry Minister Ubaldo Scavone as saying GM wants to install a plant to build "small to medium production models" in Paraguay and establish the base for a future autoparts industry in that country.

Gazeta said GM officials met with Scavone in 1996's second half to discuss the project and quoted him as saying two barriers remain: the steady flow of stolen cars into neighboring countries and indiscriminate used car imports into Paraguay.
GM officials declined to comment further on the report. "We have nothing on this," Lellis said.
The automaker has one auto plant operating in the Brazilian state of Sao Paulo state and is building a plant in Rio Grande do Sul state.
